subject: Archaeology
title: Dendrochronology: Tree-Ring Dating
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Dendrochronology: Tree-Ring Dating.

hook.text: Trees add one ring each year. Wide rings mean good years, narrow rings mean drought. The pattern is like a fingerprint.

buildup.text: By overlapping ring patterns from living and dead trees, scientists built continuous records stretching back thousands of years.

discovery.text: European oak chronologies now reach back over 10,000 years — every single year is accounted for.

twist.text: Dendrochronology can date to the exact year — sometimes even the season. No other method is this precise.

climax.text: Tree rings proved that Viking sagas were accurate. A Norse settlement in Newfoundland was dated precisely to 1021 CE.

punchline.text: A tree in Newfoundland confirmed a Viking saga. Every ring told the truth.

quiz.question: Why is dendrochronology exceptionally useful?
options: It works on all materials, not just organic ones
It can date to the exact year — sometimes even the season
It is the cheapest dating method available to archaeologists
